KNOX II at the FIBA U17 World Championship 2016|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2016/player/Kevin-Devon-Knox-II|website=FIBA.basketball|access-date=June 25, 2020}} (born August 11, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Windy City Bulls]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. Knox was selected ninth overall by the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Knox attended [[Tampa Catholic High School]] in [[Tampa, Florida]]. As a junior, he averaged 30.1 [[points per game]], 11.2 [[rebounds per game]], and 2.4 assists while leading the Crusaders to regional and district championships and runner-up to the 2016 Florida Class 4A semifinals. In the 2016 summer, he joined his AAU team, E1T1 United on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) Circuit. On May 14, 2016, Knox scored career high 28 points in a win against All Ohio Red. He averaged 19.6 points per game and 7.6 rebounds per game on the EYBL circuit. As a senior, Knox averaged 28.5 [[points per game]] and 11.3 [[rebounds per game]] leading Tampa Catholic to a (25–6) record. He played in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]]. ===Recruiting=== He was a five-star recruit and was regarded as one of the top players in the 2017 class. On May 6, 2017, Knox committed to play basketball at the University of Kentucky, spurning offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{cite news|last1=Johnson|first1=Chris|title=Four Factors That Will Define Kentucky's Season Going Forward|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/12/14/kentucky-wildcats-schedule-defense-kevin-knox-john-calipari|access-date=January 24, 2018|work=December 14, 2017}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Kevin Knox II | position = SF | hometown = [[Miami]], [[Florida]] | highschool = [[Tampa Catholic High School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 205 | 40 = | commitdate = June 5, 2017 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 95 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = | scout ref title = | espn ref title = | 247 ref title = | rivals school = | 247 school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | scout overall = #7 | rivals overall = #9 | 247 overall = #8 | espn overall = #7 | access-date = | bball = yes }} ==College career== In his freshman season, Knox led the Wildcats to a 10–8 conference record, finishing fourth in the SEC, and led the team with 15.9 points per game. He was named to the All-Rookie and First Team All-SEC teams.{{cite news|last1=Page|first1=Fletcher|title=2018 SEC Men's Basketball Awards announced|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/22657404/2018-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced|access-date=March 17, 2018|work=SEC website|date=March 6, 2017}} The team turned their fortunes around in time to win the [[SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], with Knox totaling 18 points and 7 rebounds in the final game against [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]].{{cite news|last1=Page|first1=Fletcher|title=Kentucky wins fourth straight SEC Tournament|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/22723200/kentucky-wins-fourth-straight-sec-tournament|access-date=March 17, 2018|work=SEC website|date=March 11, 2017}} In the 2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament with Virginia losing to Maryland–Baltimore County, Cincinnati losing to Nevada, Tennessee losing to Loyola-Chicago, and Buffalo beating Arizona, Kentucky was considered to have an easier path to the Final Four but Kansas State beat them, with Kevin Knox posting 13 points and 8 rebounds.{{Cite web |last=Polacek |first=Scott |date=March 23, 2018 |title=Kansas State to Play Loyola-Chicago in Elite 8 After Beating Kentucky 61–58 |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2766130-kansas-state-to-play-loyola-chicago-in-elite-8-after-beating-kentucky-61-58 |access-date=April 13, 2023 |website=bleacherreport.com}} On April 6, 2018, Knox declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] and hired an agent, forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Goodman |first=Jeff |date=April 6, 2018 |title=Kevin Knox declares for draft after one season at Kentucky |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23052912 |access-date=April 8, 2018 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} ==Professional career== ===New York Knicks (2018–2022)=== Knox was selected with the ninth overall pick by the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Iseman |first1=Chris |title=NBA Draft: New York Knicks banking on Kevin Knox's upside, potential |url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/nba/knicks/2018/06/21/new-york-knicks-take-x-nba-draft-no-x-overall/721213002/ |access-date=June 26, 2018 |publisher=[[North Jersey Media Group]] |date=June 21, 2018}} On July 5, 2018, the Knicks announced that they had signed Knox.{{cite web |last=Ballow |first=Jonah |date=July 5, 2018 |title=New York Knicks Sign Kevin Knox |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/new-york-knicks-sign-kevin-knox |access-date=April 13, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} On October 17, he made his NBA debut, coming off the bench in a 126–107 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with ten points, two steals and a block.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070697|title=Knicks overwhelm Young, Hawks 126–107 in Fizdale's debut|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2018|access-date=October 18, 2018}} Two days later, Knox scored team-high 17 points with six rebounds in a 107–105 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |date=October 20, 2018 |title=LeVert's basket gives Nets 107–105 win over Knicks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070704 |access-date=October 20, 2018 |work=ESPN.com}} One day later, he sprained his left ankle in a 103–101 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web |date=October 20, 2018 |title=Kevin Knox exits with left ankle injury, out for game |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kevin-knox-exits-ankle-injury |access-date=April 13, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} Knox returned to action and on December 1, scoring a career-high 26 points with four rebounds, four assists, a steal and a block in a 136–134 overtime win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web |date=December 1, 2018 |title=Mudiay scores 28, Knicks top Bucks 136–134 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071011 |access-date=December 2, 2018 |work=ESPN.com}} In January 2019, Knox received the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]]'s [[NBA Rookie of the Month Award]] for games played in December 2018.{{cite web |title=Kevin Knox Named KIA NBA Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/kevin-knox-named-eastern-conference-rookie-of-the-month |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 4, 2021 |date=January 3, 2019}} On January 13, 2019, he scored a career-high 31 points with seven rebounds, and two steals in a 108–105 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |date=January 13, 2019 |title=76ers escape with 108–105 win over Knicks; Embiid scores 26 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071314 |access-date=January 14, 2019 |work=ESPN.com}} On December 21, 2019, Knox recorded a season-high 19 points, alongside four rebounds, two steals and three blocks, in a 123–102 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |date=December 22, 2019 |title=Giannis has triple-double, Bucks rout Knicks 123–102 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story?id=28348881 |access-date=April 13, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} Knox's percentages dropped during his sophomore season, as he only played 17.9 minutes per game whilst averaging 6.4 points per game.{{Cite web |title=Kevin Knox Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/k/knoxke01.html |access-date=February 12, 2023 |website=Basketball Reference}} On December 21, 2020, the Knicks announced that they exercised their fourth-year option on Knox.{{cite tweet |user=NY_KnicksPR |number=1341148202192560135 |date=December 21, 2020 |title=New York Knicks announced today that the team has exercised its third-year contract option on guard/forward RJ Barrett and its fourth-year contract option on forward Kevin Knox II}} On January 11, 2021, Knox scored a season-high 19 points, alongside five rebounds and two assists, in a 109–88 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |last=Reed |first=Steve |date=January 12, 2021 |title=Hayward scores 34 points, Hornets rout Knicks 109–88 |url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-new-york-charlotte-new-orleans-pelicans-lamelo-ball-c475e4db0c93fa990d9e82a2cd7aafcd |access-date=April 13, 2023 |website=apnews.com}} During the [[2020–21 NBA season|2020–21 regular season]], the Knicks finished with a 41–31 record and qualified for the playoffs for the first time since [[2013 NBA playoffs|2013]]. The Knicks faced the [[Atlanta Hawks]] during their first-round series. Knox made his playoff debut on May 30, 2021, scoring two points in a 113–96 game 4 loss.{{Cite web |last=Newerry |first=Paul |date=May 31, 2021 |title=Young leads Hawks to 113–96 win over Knicks, 3–1 series lead |url=https://apnews.com/article/ny-state-wire-atlanta-hawks-new-york-knicks-nba-sports-1fe8f37d9b9a044c1c9ab3b53d0729c1 |access-date=April 13, 2023 |website=apnews.com}} The Knicks ended up losing the series in five games. On December 12, 2021, Knox scored a season-high 18 points, alongside five rebounds, in a 112–97 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |last=Gorman |first=Denis P. |date=December 13, 2021 |title=Balanced Bucks cruise past short-handed Knicks 112–97 |url=https://apnews.com/article/college-football-nba-sports-khris-middleton-milwaukee-bucks-98de2ae336648cd2386d4dfa78cda22f |access-date=April 13, 2023 |website=apnews.com}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2022)=== On January 13, 2022, the Knicks traded Knox and a protected future first-round pick to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for future teammate [[Cam Reddish]], [[Solomon Hill (basketball)|Solomon Hill]], a 2025 second-round pick and cash considerations.{{cite web |last=Rehmann |first=Arman |date=January 13, 2022 |title=Hawks Acquire Kevin Knox II And First-Round Pick In Exchange For Cam Reddish, Solomon Hill And Second-Round Pick |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-kevin-knox-ii-and-first-round-pick-exchange-cam-reddish-solomon-hill-and-second-round |access-date=January 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}{{cite web |title=Knicks Acquire Cam Reddish |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-acquire-cam-reddish |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 14, 2022 |date=January 13, 2022}} Knox made his Hawks debut on January 19, scoring two points in a 134–122 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web |date=January 20, 2022 |title=Young's scoring surge sends Hawks past Timberwolves, 134–122 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401360489 |access-date=April 13, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} The Hawks qualified for the postseason and faced the [[Miami Heat]] during their first-round series. On April 17, Knox scored a playoff career-high 10 points, alongside two rebounds, in a 115–91 game 1 loss.{{Cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |date=April 18, 2022 |title=Robinson makes eight 3s, Heat top Hawks 115–91 in Game 1 |url=https://apnews.com/article/miami-heat-atlanta-hawks-nba-sports-jimmy-butler-524f6e3dc3b47326af36a281e871e64d |access-date=April 13, 2023 |website=apnews.com}} He surpassed this total on April 24, scoring 12 points in a 110–86 game 4 loss.{{Cite web |title=BUTLER HAS 36 POINTS AS HEAT OVERWHELM YOUNG, HAWKS, 110–86 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100104 |access-date=February 12, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} The Hawks ended up losing the series in five games. ===Detroit Pistons (2022–2023)=== On August 1, 2022, Knox signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web|date=2022-08-01|title=Pistons re-sign Rodney McGruder, finalize Kevin Knox deal|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2022/08/01/report-pistons-re-sign-rodney-mcgruder-finalize-kevin-knox-deal/10210067002/|access-date=2022-08-02|website=DetroitNews.com|language=en-US}} He made his Pistons debut on October 19, recording three points and three rebounds in a 113–109 win over the [[2022–23 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web |last=Lage |first=Larry |date=October 20, 2022 |title=Bogdanovic shines in Detroit debut, helps Pistons beat Magic |url=https://apnews.com/article/orlando-magic-nba-sports-isaiah-stewart-jalen-duren-991a9a39b6201249338c7349576958f1 |access-date=April 13, 2023 |website=apnews.com}} On November 23, Knox scored a season-high 21 points, alongside three rebounds and a career-high six 3-pointers, in a 125–116 win over the [[2022–23 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web |last=Coles |first=Matthew |date=November 24, 2022 |title=Bogdanovic, Pistons beat Jazz for back-to-back road wins |url=https://apnews.com/article/utah-jazz-nba-sports-collin-sexton-detroit-pistons-1452b6af06f7f5383841cb9be53690ae |access-date=April 13, 2023 |website=apnews.com}} Knox made 42 appearances (including one start) for Detroit during the [[2022–23 NBA season]], recording averages of 5.6 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 0.4 assists.{{Cite web|title=Kevin Knox II 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4278075/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=August 10, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2023)=== On February 9, 2023, Knox was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in a four-team trade involving the [[Atlanta Hawks]] and [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Kevin Knox II and Five Future Second Round Picks in Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-kevin-knox-ii-and-five-future-second-round-picks-in-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}}{{cite tweet|first=C.J.|last=Holmes 🚀|title=Full terms of the Warriors' multi-team deal|number=1623878981706743808|user=CjHolmes22|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}} He made his Trail Blazers debut on February 13, recording four points and two rebounds in a 127–115 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|first=Anne M.|last=Peterson|title=Blazers hit 23 3-pointers, beat LeBron-less Lakers 127–115|url=https://apnews.com/article/los-angeles-lakers-portland-trail-blazers-nba-sports-basketball-5f5733370690adf685eba6e6e2b7c2d5|website=APNews.com|date=February 14, 2023|access-date=April 13, 2023}} On April 8, Knox scored a season-high 30 points, along with 11 rebounds, in a 136–125 loss to the [[2022–23 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |title=Portland Trail Blazers at Los Angeles Clippers Box Score, April 8, 2023 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202304080LAC.html |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=February 9, 2024}} In 21 games for the team (including four starts), he averaged 8.5 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 0.9 assists. On October 2, 2023, Knox re-signed with the Trail Blazers,{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Five Players|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-five-players|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2023|access-date=October 2, 2023}} but was waived on October 21, prior to the start of the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Convert Justin Minaya To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-convert-justin-minaya-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}} Nine days later, he joined the [[Rip City Remix]],{{cite tweet|first=Casey|last=Holdahl|title=The @ripcityremix begin training camp for their {{as written|ina|gural [sic]}} season today at the @trailblazers practice facility. Here's who they're taking into camp...|number=1719017456981696590|user=CHold|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 8, 2023}} but never played for them. ===Return to Detroit (2023–2024)=== On November 8, 2023, Knox re-signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has signed forward Kevin Knox II. Per team policy, terms of the contract were not disclosed.|number=1722356658867720402|user=Pistons_PR|date=November 8, 2023|access-date=November 8, 2023}} On January 12, 2024, Knox scored a season-high 19 points with seven rebounds in a 112–110 loss against the [[2023–24 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|title=Houston Rockets at Detroit Pistons Box Score, January 12, 2024|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202401120DET.html|work=Basketball Reference|access-date=February 9, 2024}} He played in 31 appearances (including 11 starts) for the Pistons during the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], averaging 7.2 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 0.7 assists.{{Cite web|title=Kevin Knox II 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4278075/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=August 10, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On February 8, 2024, Knox was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]], alongside a second round pick and the rights to [[Gabriele Procida]], in exchange for [[Simone Fontecchio]].{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Kevin Knox II, Future Draft Pick, and Draft Rights from Detroit Pistons|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-kevin-knox-ii-future-draft-pick-and-draft-rights-from-detroit-pistons|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} However, he was waived the next day.{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Waive Kevin Knox II|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-kevin-knox-ii|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, web|title=Warriors Sign Yuri Collins and Kevin Knox II to 10-Day
